about.title: Personal Injury Help in Corning, California
about.longDescription: Corning sits along the Interstate 5 corridor in Tehama County, where local drivers merge onto the northbound lanes near Marguerite Avenue every day heading toward Red Bluff or Redding. The most recent full-year public records for Corning showed no reported injury collisions or traffic deaths, a reassuring number for a small city of about 7,548 residents — but crashes still happen on I-5 and surface streets, and when they do, the aftermath can be overwhelming. Between insurance calls, medical appointments, and missed work, figuring out your next step shouldn't add to the stress. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Corning with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, we don't charge you anything to make the connection, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. If you were hurt in or around Corning, whether on I-5, Marguerite Avenue, or elsewhere in Tehama County, it costs nothing to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Black and White
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for an accident, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault applies to your specific situation.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means the full extent of what you've been through can be considered, not just your medical bills.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover Something
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you don't pay anything upfront and there's no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf. That structure lets you get legal help without adding financial risk while you're already dealing with an injury.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is completely free, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Any attorney you're matched with typically works on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Corning?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity, like a city or county vehicle, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your timeline sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Corning?
items.answer: Public-record collision counts show activity concentrated along Interstate 5, particularly the northbound lanes, as well as near Marguerite Avenue. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Fridays between roughly 3 and 5 a.m. These are neutral traffic patterns based on available records, not a judgment about any specific road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is different from states that bar recovery entirely if you're found more than 50% at fault.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most standard personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other types of claims, like certain medical malpractice cases, so it's worth discussing your specific situation with an attorney.
